chk_problem.reason: Both drafts identify the same core problem of addressing or predicting functional mobility decline in older adults before observable impairment or falls occur.

chk_method.reason: Both drafts describe the method as using LightGBM models with trajectory features derived from twelve routine biomarkers.

chk_data.reason: Both drafts identify the All of Us Research Program Controlled Tier Dataset version 8 with 297,861 participants.

chk_setup.reason: Both drafts describe the evaluation setup as 5-fold cross-validation comparing four machine learning algorithms.

chk_primary_result.reason: Both drafts report the same primary result of the LightGBM model with trajectory features achieving an AUROC of 0.797 and an AUPRC of 0.380.

chk_secondary_result.reason: Both drafts identify the prediction horizon analysis showing sustained prediction 3 to 12 months before onset with AUROCs ranging from 0.768 to 0.740.

chk_baseline.reason: Both drafts identify static laboratory summaries as the baseline comparison.

chk_conclusion.reason: Both drafts conclude that longitudinal trajectory features of routine biomarkers significantly improve/outperform static summaries for predicting functional mobility decline.

chk_limitation.reason: Both drafts identify limitations related to the use of ICD-10 codes for outcomes and high missingness in certain biomarkers.
